key_insight: TrialDesignBench reveals a gap between frontier LLMs and expert-validated, contemporary standards for early-phase oncology trial design.
clinical_relevance: The benchmark could support research toward AI-assisted dose-finding trial design aligned with recent FDA initiatives, including Project Optimus.
method: Paired trials with expert-validated reference designs using a formalized expert decision process.
Evaluated five frontier LLMs and tested sources of performance gaps through ablations.
evidence_signal: None of the five LLMs matched the reference standard; supplying latent design determinants increased class-wise balanced accuracy by 0.22, while structured decision-tree reasoning increased it by 0.24.
watch_item: Benchmark performance does not establish prospective clinical utility, and important design determinants may be missing from trial records.
paper_title: TrialDesignBench: Benchmarking Language Models for Phase-I Trial Design Against Clinical Knowledge
